claims.text: sgit in GitHub Actions needs its own repository and website, not a corner of another project: its own issues, its own CI pipeline, and a site that publishes what each run found.
claims.quote: That needs its own repository and its own website, not a corner of another project.

claims.text: The CI article tested the pieces locally, and its workflow file was a sketch that said so; the next step is to run it on GitHub Actions for real and keep running it.
claims.quote: Its workflow file was a sketch; it said so.

claims.text: On every run the same small build output travels from a build job to a test job and a release job four ways, in parallel.
claims.quote: the same small build output travels from a build job to a test job and a release job, four ways, in parallel

claims.text: Lane one, a vault server: the keys are in the repository's secrets, each job clones only the folders it needs with --path, and pushes back.
claims.quote: The keys are in the repository's secrets, each job clones only the folders it needs with --path, and pushes back.

claims.text: GitHub's artefacts are immutable since upload-artifact v4 and persist data after a job has completed to share with another job in the same workflow.
claims.quote: Artifacts created by upload-artifact@v4 are immutable

claims.text: GitHub artefacts are retained for 90 days by default.
claims.quote: are retained for 90 days by default

claims.text: Because the zipped vault holds only ciphertext, it can be published as a file and downloaded anywhere without the key leaving the secrets.
claims.quote: Because the zip holds only ciphertext, it can be published as a file and downloaded anywhere without the key leaving the secrets.

claims.text: Lane three, published as files: the encrypted objects on any web host, cloned read-only with sgit's static transport, which reaches any GET host; no server and no write path.
claims.quote: cloned read-only with sgit's static transport, which reaches "any GET host, read-only".

claims.text: Append lanes fill a gap in artefacts: the current upload action does not support several jobs uploading to the same artefact, and a lane takes them all.
claims.quote: the current version of the upload action does not support several jobs uploading to the same artefact. A lane takes them all.

claims.text: Each lane reports the wall time per job and run, the bytes downloaded and on disk, which keys each job held and therefore what it could have read, and a screenshot of the result.
claims.quote: which keys each job held, and therefore what it could have read; and a screenshot of the result.

claims.text: The outputs differ on purpose: a job that cloned one folder should hold one folder.
claims.quote: a job that cloned one folder should hold one folder.

claims.text: A clone of one folder barely grows with the vault: 0.59 seconds at 100 files, 0.64 at 500, 0.77 at 2,000.
claims.quote: 0.59 seconds for a 100-file vault, 0.64 at 500, 0.77 at 2,000.

value.unit: seconds for a one-folder clone of a 2,000-file vault

claims.text: A full clone grows with the vault: 0.95, 1.98 and 5.55 seconds for the same three vaults.
claims.quote: A full clone grows with the vault. 0.95, 1.98 and 5.55 seconds for the same three vaults.

value.unit: seconds for a full clone of a 2,000-file vault

claims.text: The one-folder clone downloads only that folder: 4.1 MB on disk out of 82.7 MB for the full clone of the largest vault.
claims.quote: 4.1 MB on disk out of 82.7 MB for the full clone of the largest.

value.unit: MB on disk for one folder against the full clone

claims.text: For 40 files of 3 MB each a full sgit clone took 4.4 seconds and a full git clone from local disk 16.1, most likely because git tries to compress incompressible data.
claims.quote: For 40 files of 3 MB each, a full sgit clone took 4.4 seconds; a full git clone of the same files from local disk took 16.1

value.unit: seconds for a full sgit clone of 40 files of 3 MB

claims.text: A push of a file over 4 MB failed against a server using local disk storage, because sgit sends large files through cloud storage uploads; a headless clone then could not fetch a single file.
claims.quote: A push of a file over 4 MB failed against a server using local disk storage, because sgit sends large files through cloud storage uploads.

claims.text: Ten full clones at once took 21.1 seconds on a single server process, while ten one-folder clones took 1.9.
claims.quote: ten full clones at once took 21.1 seconds on a single server process, while ten one-folder clones took 1.9.

value.unit: seconds for ten concurrent full clones on one server process

claims.text: The repository should have a budget, with every token spent by a model step counted against it per run and per provider, and the same step run on more than one provider.
claims.quote: the repository should have a budget, and every token spent should be counted against it, per run and per provider.

claims.text: A model call can happen in the job with a provider key in secrets, or in the browser inside a vault app, where the vault's key stays in the host and the frame never sees it.
claims.quote: the vault's key stays in the HOST; your frame never sees it

claims.text: Which of the two places for a model call works best in a CI run is one of the things the showcase should find out.
claims.quote: Which of the two works best in a CI run is one of the things the showcase should find out.

claims.text: The failures become issues: large files without cloud storage, a headless clone fetching a file, concurrent full clones, each with a reproduction checked on every release.
claims.quote: The failures as issues. Large files without cloud storage, a headless clone fetching a file, concurrent full clones: each an issue with a reproduction, checked on every release.

claims.text: Keys only in secrets, never in a workflow file, a log or an artefact's name; every artefact and published file is ciphertext; read keys may be published, write keys never.
claims.quote: Keys only in secrets, never in a workflow file, a log or an artefact's name.

claims.text: The budget is a hard limit, not a report after the fact.
claims.quote: And the budget is a hard limit, not a report after the fact.

claims.text: The numbers are local: one four-core machine, a local server over HTTP, three runs each; GitHub's runners and a real network will differ.
claims.quote: The numbers are local. One four-core machine, a local server over HTTP, three runs each; GitHub's runners and a real network will differ.

claims.text: Git is not a like-for-like baseline; it read local disk with no encryption and no HTTP.
claims.quote: Git is not a like-for-like baseline. It read local disk with no encryption and no HTTP.

claims.text: Lanes 2 and 3, the artefact and static lanes, are untested and built from the documentation; lanes 1 and 4 were tested locally for the CI article.
claims.quote: Lanes 2 and 3 are untested. The artefact and static lanes are built from the documentation; lanes 1 and 4 were tested locally for the CI article.

claims.text: Nothing in the brief is built.
claims.quote: Nothing in the brief is built.

claims.text: The measurements were run by a research agent on one machine with sgit 0.21.0, version 0.34.0 of the vault server and git 2.43.0; the brief was written by the writer agent for the owner.
claims.quote: The measurements were run for this article by a research agent on one machine, with sgit 0.21.0, version 0.34.0 of the vault server and git 2.43.0.
